/-- **The `Fin`-indexed basic-open cover data** of the two pinned charts of the relative
curve (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §1a): `m₀ + m₁` basic-open generators with partition
witnesses. The DAT-1 datum `BasicOpenCoverData` carries `Type u` index fields and hence
lives in `Type (u+1)`; this `Fin`-indexed form is the `Type u` carrier a functor value
can quotient. -/
structure FinCoverData [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
  /-- The number of chart-0 pieces. -/
  m₀ : ℕ
  /-- The number of chart-1 pieces. -/
  m₁ : ℕ
  /-- The chart-0 basic-open generators. -/
  h₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
  /-- The chart-1 basic-open generators. -/
  h₁ : Fin m₁ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
  /-- The chart-0 partition coefficients. -/
  a₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
  /-- The chart-1 partition coefficients. -/
  a₁ : Fin m₁ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
  /-- The chart-0 partition witness. -/
  partition₀ : ∑ j : Fin m₀, a₀ j * h₀ j = 1
  /-- The chart-1 partition witness. -/
  partition₁ : ∑ j : Fin m₁, a₁ j * h₁ j = 1

variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] (D : FinCoverData C R π)

/-- The gluing index of the adaptation, `Fin m₀ ⊕ Fin m₁`. -/

/-- The pieces: the basic opens `D(h_j)` of the two pinned charts. -/
noncomputable def pieces : D.index → (relCurve C R).Opens :=
  Sum.elim (fun j => (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₀ j))
    (fun j => (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₁ j))

@[simp]
lemma pieces_inl (j : Fin D.m₀) :
    D.pieces (Sum.inl j) = (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₀ j) := rfl

@[simp]
lemma pieces_inr (j : Fin D.m₁) :

/-- The chart-0 pieces cover the pinned chart `V₀ᴿ`. -/

  le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one D.a₁ D.h₁ D.partition₁

/-- The chart-local colength module `Γ(D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_j)`, an `R`-algebra through

noncomputable abbrev colength (j : A.index) : Type u :=

/-- The symmetric overlap ideal: both equations restricted to the piece overlap. The
two restrictions generate the same ideal (the equations differ by units on overlaps
through the refinement witness), but the symmetric span needs no transport in the
DEFINITION. -/
noncomputable abbrev ovlIdeal (i j : A.index) :
    Ideal Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) :=
  Ideal.span
    {relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i),
     relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j)}

/-- The overlap colength module `Γ(D(h_i) ⊓ D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_i, f_j)`. -/
noncomputable abbrev ovlColength (i j : A.index) : Type u :=
  Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) ⧸ A.ovlIdeal i j

  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/

8	/-!
9	# swallow-adapt on the widened cover: the straddling piece
10	
11	Roadmap leaf `AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.swallow-adapt`, restated over
12	`AffCoverData`.  The chart-pair version (`DivSchemeCertZarChartPair.lean`) is landed but
13	consumes chart principality, which is false for an arbitrary degree-`n` divisor on a curve of
14	genus `≥ 1` (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3 corrigendum C4(i)): `Cl(V_b) ≠ 0` and
15	shrinking `Spec R` does not change a fibre class.  Over a widened cover the shape is
16	different and the obstruction does not arise: **one piece swallows the support and every
17	other piece misses it.**
18	
19	## The geometric input, supplied as a HYPOTHESIS and not re-derived
20	
21	The decision (I-0492 clause 2) says to USE, not re-derive: `supp D` is finite over `R`, hence
22	lies in a single affine open of `C ×_k Spec R` (Stacks `0B8B`).  Mathlib has no form of
23	`0B8B`, and this project constructs no curve other than `P¹`, so formalising it is out of
24	scope for this lane.  It therefore appears here as the named, explicit hypothesis
25	`SwallowedBy` — a *statement to be supplied by the seed*, exactly as
26	`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3 C4(ii) requires: the geometric input is relocated into a
27	visible obligation rather than hidden inside a `LocalEquations` or an adaptation field.
28	
29	`SwallowedBy` is deliberately NOT bundled into `AffCoverData` or `AffAdaptation`.  A reader
30	can see, from any theorem's signature, whether it assumes confinement.
31	
32	## What the shape buys
33	
34	For a cover with a straddling piece, swallow-or-miss holds by construction rather than by a
35	connectivity argument, so — with no fibre, no tube, and no packet idempotent —
36	`hnoLeak` holds at every piece, clause (c1)-finite holds at every piece, and every
37	non-swallowing piece contributes a vanishing colength (`cert-collapse`).  Crucially there is
38	no dichotomy step, hence no appeal to `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤`, hence no chart.
39	
40	## Main declarations
41	
42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffCoverData.SwallowedBy` — the straddling-piece hypothesis.
43	* `AffAdaptation.forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_swallowedBy` — swallow-or-miss from it.
44	* `AffAdaptation.forall_noLeak_of_swallowedBy` — the assembler's `hnoLeak`.
45	* `AffAdaptation.forall_finite_colength_of_swallowedBy` — clause (c1)-finite everywhere.
46	* `AffCoverData.ofSwallowingPiece` — the two-piece widened cover from a straddling affine
47	  open together with an affine open cover of the rest.
48	-/

61	
62	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
63	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
64	
65	namespace AffCoverData
66	
67	/-- **The straddling-piece hypothesis** (the Stacks `0B8B` input, supplied not derived): some
68	piece of the cover contains the whole support locus, and every other piece is disjoint from
69	it.
70	
71	This is the widened replacement for "the support lies in `V₀ ⊓ V₁`".  The difference that
72	matters: `V₀ ⊓ V₁` is the complement of a FIXED PAIR of vertical fibres and provably cannot
73	always be arranged (ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 exhibits a straddling divisor at every genus `≥ 2`),
74	whereas an affine open containing a support finite over `R` always exists. -/
75	def SwallowedBy (D : AffCoverData C R) (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) : Prop :=
76	  ∃ j₀ : D.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (D.pieces j₀ : Set (relCurve C R)) ∧
77	    ∀ j : D.index, j ≠ j₀ → Disjoint d.supportLocus (D.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))

9	# cert-collapse on the widened cover: the diagonal is degenerate, and what that forces
10	
11	Roadmap leaf `AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.cert-collapse`, restated over
12	`AffCoverData`.  The leaf's ORIGINAL claim — that (c2)/(c3)/(c4) are FREE for a
13	swallow-or-miss adaptation — was **refuted** by work-reviewer at I-0340 and must not be
14	re-derived.  This file lands the structural fact behind the refutation, and the corrected
15	positive statement, on the widened structure.
16	
17	## The refutation, now kernel-checked rather than argued
18	
19	`toOvlLeft i i = toOvlRight i i` holds by `rfl`: at `pieces i ⊓ pieces i` proof irrelevance
20	makes `inf_le_left` and `inf_le_right` the same proof, so the two arrows are literally the
21	same map (`toOvl_diag_eq`).  Hence **every diagonal component of `deltaLeft - deltaRight`
22	is identically zero** (`deltaSub_apply_diag`), for every adaptation over every cover.
23	
24	The consequence, which is why "free" is false: the cokernel of the difference arrow always
25	retains the diagonal factor `∏_i ovlColength i i`, so clause (c4) forces flatness of those
26	overlap colengths — it can never be discharged by a structural observation about which
27	pieces meet the support.  `away-kerspan` therefore stays blocked rather than rejected.
28	
29	## The corrected positive statement
30	
31	What survives is a REDUCTION, not a retirement: on a swallow-or-miss adaptation every piece
32	either swallows the support or misses it, and a missing piece contributes a VANISHING
33	colength and vanishing overlap colengths (`subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus`,
34	`subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint`).  A subsingleton module is free of rank zero, hence
35	flat and projective, so all the missing-piece factors are free of content and only the
36	swallowing pieces carry the certificate — at most one per connected component of the
37	support, rather than one per chart.
38	
39	## Main declarations
40	
41	* `AffAdaptation.toOvl_diag_eq` — the two overlap arrows agree on the diagonal, by `rfl`.
42	* `AffAdaptation.deltaSub_apply_diag` — every diagonal component of the difference vanishes.
43	* `AffAdaptation.subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint` — a piece missing the support kills
44	  its overlap colengths too.
45	* `AffAdaptation.flat_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus`,
46	  `projective_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus` — the missing-piece clauses (c1), free of
47	  any fibrewise-regularity input.
48	-/

## Why it is nearly free, and where the one real step is

`toAffCoverData.pieces j` is *definitionally* `D.pieces (finSumFinEquiv.symm j)`, so the
section rings, the equations, the colength modules, the overlap ideals and both overlap arrows

The one real step is the glued clauses (c2)/(c3)/(c4): `gluedSubmodule` is a kernel inside

proofs from drowning in `Eq.mpr`s.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.toAff` — the widened adaptation of a chart-typed one.
* `DivisorAdaptation.gluedCongr` — the glued modules agree, along `piCongrLeft.symm`.
* `DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_toAff` — the certificate migrates, all seven clauses.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamily.toAff` — the certified family migrates.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_isLocallyCertified` — the chart-typed pin
